title: Communication in getting to know someone
summary:
When two people meet and build a relationship, they exchange a variety of social signals, for example through eye contact, gestures, and facial expressions. In digital encounters—such as video calls—this process may be slightly different. The reason is that we perceive our counterpart through a screen and are therefore unable to fully grasp some of the signals that are effective in a face-to-face meeting.
We are interested in how such digital encounters affect communication between two people. In addition, we are investigating whether certain physical processes, such as the activity of the body's own hormone oxytocin, which plays a decisive role in controlling our face-to-face social behavior, could be altered in digital encounters. The administration of the nasal spray has no clinical or therapeutic purpose, but is used exclusively for basic research.
The aim of the study is therefore to better understand how communication takes place when people get to know each other in digital situations and what influence oxytocin has on this.
conditions: This study examines the influence of oxytocin on gaze behavior in digital interactions among healthy individuals.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Very good knowledge of German language
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals need to be excluded, if they are currently diagnosed mental illness or if they have ongoing neurological, psychiatric, or psychotherapeutic treatment. We will also exclude individuals with the use of hormonally active (endocrine) or psychoactive medications, either currently within the last 48 hours before the experiment or on a permanent basis. This includes, for example, psychotropic drugs such as neuroleptics, antidepressants, tranquilizers, or sleeping pills. In terms of eye tracking, individuals with visual impairment greater than +3 or less than -3 diopters, allergic reactions affecting the eyes, or eyelid disorders will be excluded. Individuals with an acute common cold or an allergy to preservatives in nasal sprays (parabens) or illness for the nasal mucosa will be excluded.
